steps.body: Some sums need two trades. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten, then trade 10 tens for 1 hundred.
steps.narration: Some sums need two trades. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten, then trade 10 tens for 1 hundred.

widget.prompt: Start with 4 flats, 11 rods, and 13 cubes. Make the two trades to show 523.

commonBuilds.feedback: Twelve rods still need a trade. Trade 10 tens for 1 flat.

widget.missFeedback: That build names a different number — total each unit's worth and match 523 exactly.
widget.successFeedback: Five flats, 2 rods, and 3 cubes show both trades are complete.

predict.prompt: Ones trade AND tens trade: which happens first working right to left?
predict.reveal: Right-to-left order means the ones bundle first — and that new ten joins the tens before THEY bundle.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2b two trades.
invariants: Trading between places changes the form of a quantity, never its value — the model and the number must stay equal for g2b two trades.
misconceptions: Treating a trade as adding or removing amount instead of renaming the same total.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the blocks stop matching the written number?

explanationVariants: Each carry feeds the next column.

commonErrors.feedback: Both trades went missing — the new ten AND the new hundred must be carried.
The ones trade landed but the tens trade did not — bundle those ten tens into a hundred.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the places up — hundreds with hundreds, tens with tens, ones with ones — and work one column at a time.

hints: Ten of a small unit equal one of the next.
Bundle them and move them left.

widget.prompt: While solving with 355, a student trades ten ones for a ten. Why is that allowed?

options.label: Because ten ones and one ten are equal amounts
options.feedback: Correct — the trade is legal exactly because both forms name the same quantity.

options.label: Because the answer gets bigger
options.feedback: A valid trade never changes the total at all — that is the whole point of it.

options.label: Because tens look nicer than ones
options.feedback: Looks are not the reason; equal VALUE is what licenses the swap.

options.label: Because subtraction requires it every time
options.feedback: Many subtractions need no trade; the trade appears only when a place runs short.
